title: Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions, Part II
summary: Plan the Schwartz multiplier method for isolating automorphic cuspidal components, together with the weighted quotient spaces and Schwartz spectral-kernel interfaces on which it acts. Entire interpolation controls growth on real-form spectral lattices; local multipliers, polynomial cuspidal counting and finite-place Hecke separation produce global normalized annihilators. The plan imports existing functional analysis, automorphic representations, reduction theory and compact spectral decomposition, records exact missing supplier contracts, and routes the already planned congruence spectral gap to its existing owner.
readme:
This continuation owns Schwartz multipliers, weighted automorphic quotient spaces, their spectral-kernel interfaces and isolation of cuspidal components. Let F be a number field and G a connected reductive F-group. For global isolation let Z be its maximal F-split central torus and ω a unitary automorphic character of Z(𝔸). Fix a minimal parabolic, standard Levis, an admissible maximal compact K₀ and compatible Haar/quotient measures from AA. At each unramified finite place vol(K₀,v)=1. Finite S contains the bad group/level places, T is any set of finite places with S⊂T, and K=K_S×∏_{v∉S}K₀,v. T can be infinite, but each Hecke tensor uses finitely many places. Induction is normalized; infinitesimal characters are W-orbits in the complexified abstract Cartan dual. Cuspidal data and orthogonal components are those of AS.1/AS.4, compared through R6 and R9.

Write [G]_P=M_P(F)N_P(𝔸)\G(𝔸), [G]=[G]_G, and use the proper height n_P≥1. Derivatives R(X) are from the right regular action. On real groups L(X)f(g)=(d/dt)₀ f(exp(−tX)g). In the paper’s linear-first pairing write ⟨φ,ψ⟩=∫φ·conj(ψ); when translating to Mathlib’s conjugate-first inner product interchange the slots. Adjoints use f*(g)=conj(f(g⁻¹)) with the unimodular Haar normalization. A quotient by A_P∞ and the normalized δ_P^{1/2} action are used only where explicitly stated. The split centre is not silently discarded.

All smooth adelic spaces have a locally constant finite-place action. Test Schwartz functions at finite places are compactly supported, while real test functions have Nash (algebraic differential operator) decay. S(G(𝔸)) is the existing AF.0 convolution algebra. S([G]_P) and C([G]_P) are quotient function spaces. Neither is identified with local Harish-Chandra Schwartz functions by notation alone. All topological sums and completed tensor products keep their indicated topology. The roadmap gives mathematical targets; every implementation status is unchecked.

SM.0. Entire interpolation and real-form symbol algebras. Construct finite-order zero sets and vertical interpolation, fix the finite real-form involution set, and build the moderate, rapid and sharp symbol algebras. Polynomial-preserving rational difference operators and their division estimates supply the derivative control used by the multiplier proof.

SM.1. Multipliers of the real and adelic Schwartz algebras. Import the AF.0 test-function carrier, compare its real stages to Nash Schwartz functions, extend Delorme’s rapid-symbol action across the connected centre, and use Kostant difference operators and Plancherel estimates to obtain all moderate-symbol multipliers. Sharp symbols detect finitely many K-types. Compare finite-place support/level stages without redefining the adelic algebra.

SM.2. Weighted automorphic function spaces and constant terms. Build quotient weights, parabolic depths and the quotient-volume function. Define weighted smooth L², rapid, Harish-Chandra, tempered-measure and partially rapid spaces, retaining AF.0 ownership of uniform moderate growth. Establish Sobolev evaluation, nuclear inclusions, product tensors, weighted constant terms, pseudo-Eisenstein extensions and cusp approximation, including graph and open-surjection statements.

SM.3. Schwartz spectral decompositions and automorphic kernels. Extend the existing cuspidal-data decomposition to the weighted function spaces, with exact summability and common-height-loss quantifiers. Prove Schwartz relative-character convergence, Arthur factorization, regular constant-term bounds and the GL_n regular-data Lapid expansion. Extend automorphic kernels and their grouped Eisenstein spectral expansions to Schwartz tests with uniform weight bounds.

SM.4. Typical cuspidal data and finite archimedean selection. Define T-characters, CAP characters, T-multipliers and quasi-cuspidality. Use both the compact-central condition and derived Casimir condition for typical data. Obtain finite-rank Casimir values, finite typical data and sharp archimedean annihilators of all but finitely many coarse cuspidal components.

SM.5. Mixed multipliers and isolation of cuspidal components. Define simultaneous occurrence at infinity and every retained finite place. Construct mixed annihilators, normalize at the target character, and isolate occurring components. Deduce non-CAP isolation, isolation within the cuspidal domain, preservation of a non-CAP admissible representation, the single GL_n cuspidal-support component, and the discrete-data refinement subject to its explicit counting contract.

The congruence spectral gap is already owned by CongruenceSpectralGap and is routed to that existing roadmap. Relative trace formulae, transfer and Gan–Gross–Prasad periods consume these analytic results and remain with their existing owners.

stages.title: Entire interpolation and real-form symbol algebras
stages.description: Construct finite-order zero sets and vertical interpolation, fix the finite real-form involution set, and build the moderate, rapid and sharp symbol algebras. Polynomial-preserving rational difference operators and their division estimates supply the derivative control used by the multiplier proof. Targets: Finite-rank subsets of the complex line: For Λ⊂ℂ and p∈ℕ, hasRankBound(Λ,p) means Λ is countable and Σ_{λ∈Λ,λ≠0} ‖λ‖^{−(p+1)} converges. HasFiniteRank means some such p exists; rank is the least such p. The possible zero of Λ is omitted from the sum and is recorded separately in the canonical product.; Finite-order Weierstrass products: If Λ has finite rank p, let E_p(w)=(1−w)exp(Σ_{j=1}^p w^j/j) and δ=1 if 0∈Λ, otherwise 0. The products z^δ∏_{λ∈Λ\{0}}E_p(z/λ) converge normally on compact sets to an entire function ΨΛ, with zero set exactly Λ and simple zeros there; its order is at most p+1. Finite order here means a global bound exp(C(1+‖z‖)^d) for some positive C and integer d, which is equivalent to the usual finiteness of entire order.; Interpolation with vertical strip decay: Let U be a finite-dimensional real vector space, Ψ an entire function on ℂ of finite order, and q:Uℂ→ℂ polynomial. There is an entire ν with exactly the zero set q^{-1}(Ψ^{-1}(0)) and with rapid decay on every vertical strip: for every M>0 and r∈ℕ, sup_{‖Re z‖≤M}(1+‖z‖)^r|ν(z)|<∞. Consequently this holds for q^{-1}(Λ) when Λ has finite rank. If L⊂Uℂ is generated by complex-linearly independent vectors and A⊂Uℂ is finite, there is such a vertically moderate ν vanishing on L\A and nonzero at every point of A; no vanishing requirement is imposed off L. The same conclusion holds for an affine translate of L, by translating the variable and the finite exceptional set. This is not asserted for an arbitrary lattice of the underlying real space of Uℂ.; Real-form involutions and shifted lattices: Import a based root datum (X*,Φ,X_*,Φ∨), its finite Weyl group W and real Cartan dual h*=X*⊗ℝ. For a real form choose its action ϑ₀ on the datum and put θ={wϑ₀:w∈W,(wϑ₀)²=1}; this finite W-conjugation-stable set is the real-form set. For ϑ∈θ let h*ϑ and h*−ϑ be its ±1 eigenspaces and Yϑ=pr_{−ϑ}(ρ+X*), a discrete affine lattice in h*−ϑ. For each maximal real torus the split/compact decomposition gives an involution in θ; θG is the subset realized by such tori. Abstract Cartan identifications are taken modulo W.; Moderate spectral symbols: For a finite W-stable involution set Θ, define p_{ϑ,M,r}(μ)=sup_{α∈h*ϑ,ℂ,‖Re α‖≤M; ϖ∈Yϑ}|μ(α+ϖ)|(1+‖α+ϖ‖)^r, allowing value ∞. MΘ consists of entire μ for which every ϑ∈Θ and M>0 admit some real r with p finite. Equivalently use a polynomial upper bound of some nonnegative integral degree on each strip. M denotes M_{ {1} }. The invariant subalgebra is MΘ^W. Exponents may depend on ϑ and M; the bound is uniform over all lattice translates.; Rapid spectral symbols: NΘ consists of entire μ such that p_{ϑ,M,r}(μ)<∞ for every ϑ∈Θ, M>0 and real r; integral r≥0 suffice. When 1∈Θ the topology uses the countable family M,r∈ℕ with M≥1 and is Fréchet, and NΘ is an ideal in MΘ in the sense that multiplying a rapid symbol by a moderate symbol remains rapid. N denotes N_{ {1} }. Invariant symbols form the closed W-fixed subspace.; Sharp spectral symbols: M♯θ is the subalgebra of M_{θ∪{1}} consisting of μ such that, for each ϑ∈θ, the function α↦μ(α+ϖ) is identically zero on h*ϑ,ℂ for all but finitely many ϖ∈Yϑ. This is support of restrictions, not support of the entire function as a function on h*ℂ. M♯θ is an M-module. Its W-fixed algebra can be nonunital; 1 fails the condition whenever an infinite Yϑ occurs.; Sharp symbols nonzero on prescribed orbits: For every a∈h*ℂ there exists μ∈(M♯θ)^W with μ(a)≠0, provided θ is finite and W-stable. One can normalize μ(a)=1. More generally a finite set of points can be kept nonzero. No assertion is made for an infinite involution set.; Polynomial and rational difference operators: Let R=ℂ[h*ℂ]⋊(X*⋊W) act by finite sums of polynomial coefficients times affine pullbacks; fix t_λ f(α)=f(α−λ). Let T be its localization to rational coefficients and S the subalgebra obtained by inverting affine reflection linear equations ℓ_s. Write S_pol for those elements preserving all polynomials. Evaluation and composition retain the pullback order. Only finite sums occur.; Holomorphic extension and strip estimates: Every S∈S_pol extends uniquely to a continuous operator on entire functions with their compact-open topology. There are M_S>0 and a real exponent shift r_S≥0 such that, for all M>0,r∈ℝ, p_{1,M,r}(Sμ)≤C p_{1,M+M_S,r+r_S}(μ); the analogous maximum over θ holds for a real-form coset θ. A rational-coefficient difference operator preserving polynomials has poles only along affine reflection hyperplanes and belongs to S. If μ vanishes on H_s, μ/ℓ_s is entire and satisfies the corresponding widened-strip estimate without an extra polynomial exponent.

stages.title: Multipliers of the real and adelic Schwartz algebras
stages.description: Import the AF.0 test-function carrier, compare its real stages to Nash Schwartz functions, extend Delorme’s rapid-symbol action across the connected centre, and use Kostant difference operators and Plancherel estimates to obtain all moderate-symbol multipliers. Sharp symbols detect finitely many K-types. Compare finite-place support/level stages without redefining the adelic algebra. Targets: Real Schwartz and Sobolev descriptions: Take the real-group factor of AF.0/adelic-schwartz-space. Its elements are smooth functions for which Df is bounded for every algebraic differential operator D on G(ℝ). The seminorm topology is nuclear Fréchet and equals the topology defined by ‖Df‖₂ for all algebraic D, using distributional derivatives for the converse. The comparison is with Nash Schwartz functions, not merely Harish-Chandra C²(G). There is a continuous inclusion S(G)⊂⋂_{p>0}C^p(G), with equality precisely when the algebraic centre of G is compact at the real points. For an additive real vector group the resulting polynomial derivative conditions agree with Mathlib SchwartzMap.; Schwartz integration on moderate representations: For a smooth moderate-growth Fréchet representation V of G(ℝ), the integral π(f)v=∫_G f(g)π(g)v dg converges in V for f∈S(G) and defines a continuous bilinear action S(G)×V→V. It satisfies π(f₁*f₂)=π(f₁)π(f₂), left/right differentiation identities with L(X)f(g)=d/dt f(exp(−tX)g), and agreement with the compactly supported integrated action. For irreducible admissible π use its Casselman–Wallach globalization. Equality of the transforms on all such π detects an element of S(G).; Delorme multipliers for reductive real groups: For μ∈N(h*ℂ)^W and compactly supported smooth bi-K-finite f on a real reductive algebraic group, there is a unique bi-K-finite Schwartz function μ⋆f with π(μ⋆f)=μ(χπ)π(f) for every irreducible admissible π. For every fixed finite left/right K-type set and compact-support stage, the map is continuous to the corresponding finite-K-type Schwartz space. The output need not be compactly supported. The W-invariance hypothesis is mandatory.; Kostant centralizers and translated characters: For a finite-dimensional algebraic representation τ of G, Rτ=(U(g)⊗End τ)^{δg} is finite free over Z(g), and after a basis is chosen δ(z)=Σ_i S_i(z)v_i with S_i∈S_pol. If Λ(τ) is the finite weight set and t_λf(α)=f(α−λ), then ∏_{λ∈Λ(τ)}(δ(z)−t_{−λ}z)=0: its roots are α↦z(α+λ). The resulting difference operators have the strip estimates of SM.0. Freeness and this annihilator are Kostant inputs, requested from AF.1 rather than redeveloping enveloping-algebra representation theory here.; Generic semisimplicity after tensoring: For a minimal parabolic P=MAN, finite-dimensional algebraic τ, and an irreducible representation ξ of the compact-mod-centre M, the principal-series family I_P(ξ,λ)⊗τ is semisimple for λ outside a locally finite exceptional union of affine analytic hyperplanes. Its constituents have the translated infinitesimal characters prescribed by the weights of τ. The assertion is generic, not at every singular inducing parameter.; L² estimates for rapid-symbol multipliers: For μ∈N_{θ∪{1}}^W the compact-support multiplier extends uniquely to a continuous multiplier on S(G). For each algebraic differential operator D there is M_D>0 such that for every r∈ℝ a continuous seminorm ν_{D,r} on S(G) satisfies ‖D(μ⋆f)‖₂≤ν_{D,r}(f) max_{ϑ∈θ∪{1}}p_{ϑ,M_D,r}(μ). The transform identity holds on every irreducible admissible representation, not only the tempered dual.; Schwartz multipliers of moderate symbols: For every μ∈M_{θ∪{1}}(h*ℂ)^W there is a unique continuous complex-linear Tμ:S(G)→S(G) such that π(Tμf)=μ(χπ)π(f) for all irreducible admissible π. It is a centroid multiplier: Tμ(f₁*f₂)=Tμ(f₁)*f₂=f₁*Tμ(f₂). The map μ↦Tμ is multiplicative and linear, preserves every finite left/right K-type subspace, and agrees with the AS.6 compact multiplier on the common domain. Its kernel consists of symbols vanishing at actual infinitesimal characters of irreducible admissible representations; no classification of all continuous multipliers is asserted.; Finite K-type detection for sharp symbols: For μ∈(M♯θ)^W there is a finite set 𝔗 of irreducible K-types such that every irreducible admissible π with μ(χπ)≠0 contains a type in 𝔗. Moreover μ⋆ preserves bi-K-finiteness and defines the corresponding multiplier on the algebraic K-finite Schwartz algebra. This does not say μ selects finitely many irreducible representations or finitely many split inducing parameters.; Adelic LF and finite-place compatibility: Import S(G(𝔸_F)) from AF.0: at fixed compact finite support C and compact open J it is the Fréchet space of smooth bi-J-invariant functions with every seminorm sup_g ‖g‖^r|R(X)L(Y)f(g)| finite. Identify that stage with a finite direct sum of S(G∞), one copy per finite J-double coset in C. The countable support/level exhaustion is strict LF, convolution is continuous on the appropriate pairs of stages, and C_c∞ is dense. For a finite place set S, S(G(F_S)) is the completed product over real places tensored with locally constant compactly supported finite-place functions; it embeds by hyperspecial units away from S. Different embeddings obey the Hecke normalization vol(K_v)=1.

stages.title: Weighted automorphic function spaces and constant terms
stages.description: Build quotient weights, parabolic depths and the quotient-volume function. Define weighted smooth L², rapid, Harish-Chandra, tempered-measure and partially rapid spaces, retaining AF.0 ownership of uniform moderate growth. Establish Sobolev evaluation, nuclear inclusions, product tensors, weighted constant terms, pseudo-Eisenstein extensions and cusp approximation, including graph and open-surjection statements. Targets: Weights on automorphic quotients: For a standard parabolic P put [G]_P=M_P(F)N_P(𝔸)\G(𝔸), with the AA quotient measure. A weight is a positive measurable w:[G]_P→ℝ_{>0} such that for every compact U⊂G(𝔸) there is C_U≥1 with C_U^{-1}w(x)≤w(xu)≤C_Uw(x) for all x and u∈U. Write w≍w′ for two-sided global constant comparison. Every weight satisfies w(xg)≤Cw(x)‖g‖^N for some C,N and all x,g. Import the proper quotient height n_P(x)=inf_{p∈M_P(F)N_P(𝔸)}‖px‖≥1 and put σ_P=1+log n_P.; Franke weights and chamber order: For each λ∈a*₀ construct a weight d_{P,λ} on [G]_P, determined up to ≍, that is comparable with exp⟨λ,H₀(x)⟩ on every standard P-Siegel domain. It obeys d_{P,tλ}≍d_{P,λ}^t, d_{P,λ+η}≍d_{P,λ}d_{P,η}, and d_{P,λ}≪d_{P,η} if λ≺_Pη in the chamber order. For a proper embedding height, n_P≍max_{λ∈Λ^P_ι}d_{P,λ}. If λ is P-dominant, d_{P,λ}(x)≍sup_{γ∈P(F)}exp⟨λ,H₀(γx)⟩. For Q⊂P and P-dominant λ one has d_{Q,λ}≪d_{P,λ} on their common intermediate quotient.; Parabolic depth functions: For proper standard P⊊Q define d_P^Q=min_{α∈Σ_P^Q}d_{P,α} and d_Q^P=min_{α∈Σ_P^Q}d_{Q,α}, where Σ_P^Q is the finite nonempty root set in n_P/n_Q. On P(F)N_Q(𝔸)\G(𝔸), d_P^Q≪d_Q^P. Write ω_P^Q(C)={d_P^Q>C}. These are neighborhoods of infinity in the relevant parabolic directions. Their finite-fiber and deep-cusp comparison properties are imported from AA.3. If H⊂G is reductive and P∩H⊊Q∩H are parabolics with the intersected unipotent radicals, restriction satisfies d_P^Q(h)≪d_{P∩H}^{Q∩H}(h); for restriction of scalars along a finite field extension with diagonal H this is an equivalence. Treat P=Q by the identity case of subsequent theorems, not by an empty minimum.; The quotient Harish-Chandra volume function: Choose a compact identity neighborhood U⊂G(𝔸) and define Ξ_P(x)=vol_{[G]_P}(xU)^{−1/2}. Different U give equivalent positive weights. One has Ξ_P≍d_{P,ρ₀}, Ξ_P≪n_P^N for some N, and ∫_[G]_P Ξ_P(x)²σ_P(x)^{−d₀}dx<∞ for some d₀≥0. This is the quotient volume function; it is different from the local spherical Harish-Chandra Ξ of a real or p-adic group.; Smooth LF representations: An adelic SLF representation V is a smooth G(𝔸_f)-representation with V=⋃_J V^J; each V^J has an SF Fréchet representation structure for G∞, the inclusions for J′⊂J are closed topological embeddings, and V has their locally convex inductive-limit topology. The group action and stage transitions must be compatible. Use AF.1 for SF representations. A closed invariant subspace with its induced topology is SLF; continuous equivariant maps with closed image induce topological isomorphisms from the quotient by their kernels onto the image. A map need not be injective merely because its image is closed. The Schwartz action extends the compactly supported action and V∞=S(G(𝔸))·V for an F-representation before taking smooth vectors.; Smooth vectors in weighted L²: For a weight w let L²_w([G]_P)=Lp(ℂ,2,w,dx), using the almost-everywhere quotient. Right translation is a continuous moderate representation; its smooth vectors at level J consist exactly of the smooth right-J-invariant functions with R(X)φ∈L²_w for every X∈U(g∞), topologized by those derivative norms. Put L²_{N,w}=L²_{n_P^Nw} and L²_{σ,d,w}=L²_{σ_P^dw}. Pointwise representatives are the unique smooth representatives, not arbitrary representatives of Lp classes. Integration pairs L²_w with L²_{w^{-1}} sesquilinearly.; Weighted Sobolev evaluation and smoothing: At each finite level J and for every weight w there is a continuous seminorm q on L²_w([G]_P)^{∞,J} such that |φ(x)|≤q(φ)Ξ_P(x)w(x)^{−1/2} for all x. Every continuous functional T on smooth L²_w and every f∈S(G(𝔸)) is regularized to a smooth vector in L²_{w^{-1}}, characterized by T(R(f)ψ)=⟨ψ,φ⟩_P with the adjoint/inversion convention fixed by this equality. The map is continuous on fixed Schwartz stages.; Nuclear weighted inclusions: There exists d₀≥0 depending only on the quotient geometry such that for every compact open J and every weight w the inclusion L²_{σ,d₀,w}([G]_P)^{∞,J}→L²_w([G]_P)^{∞,J} is nuclear. Hence an unconditionally summable family in the source becomes absolutely summable in every continuous target seminorm. Nuclearity concerns the smooth Fréchet spaces; it does not assert that the zeroth-order weighted Hilbert inclusion alone is nuclear.; Zeroth-order rapid spaces: S₀([G]_P) consists of measurable functions with sup_x n_P(x)^N|φ(x)|<∞ for every N≥0; use actual functions for these suprema. S₀⁰ is its subspace of continuous functions with the same Fréchet seminorms. The continuous subspace is an F-representation. The full measurable S₀ is an auxiliary locally convex space; its translation action is not asserted strongly continuous. Compact smooth functions embed into both.; Schwartz functions on automorphic quotients: S([G]_P) is the smooth adelic space of functions with q_{N,X}(φ)=sup_x n_P(x)^N|R(X)φ(x)|<∞ for every N≥0 and X∈U(g∞). At fixed J it is nuclear Fréchet; over J it is strict LF. It identifies topologically with (S₀⁰)^∞ and with ⋂_{N>0}L²_{n_P^N}^{∞}, using the projective smooth topology. It is dense in every smooth L²_w space. This quotient space is distinct from the test-function convolution algebra S(G(𝔸)); the latter acts on it by right convolution.; Harish-Chandra Schwartz functions on quotients: C([G]_P) consists of smooth functions with sup_x Ξ_P(x)^{-1}σ_P(x)^d|R(X)φ(x)|<∞ for every d≥0 and X. At each J it is nuclear Fréchet and equals ⋂_{d>0}L²_{σ_P^d}^{∞,J} topologically; its level union is strict LF. The inclusion S([G]_P)→C([G]_P) is continuous with dense image. This is the global quotient Harish-Chandra space, with logarithmic decay relative to Ξ_P.; Polynomially weighted measures: T₀,w([G]_P) is the Banach space of complex Radon measures μ with ∫w^{-1}d|μ|<∞. T₀=⋃_{N≥0}T₀,n_P^N has its locally convex inductive-limit topology, which need not be strict; it identifies with the continuous sesquilinear dual of S₀⁰ using the conjugation convention of the integral pairing. Measures are not assumed absolutely continuous. Translation is bounded locally uniformly in the group variable, but is not in general strongly continuous in weighted total variation. Define convolution on measures by integration against test functions, and take norm-smooth orbit vectors only where that regularity holds. If w is bounded on supp μ then R(f)μ belongs to S_w for every Schwartz f, with the compatible continuous smoothing estimates.; Weighted uniform derivative growth: For a weight w, T_w([G]_P) consists of smooth functions with sup_x w(x)^{-1}|R(X)φ(x)|<∞ for every X, at fixed J with its Fréchet topology and then its strict level LF topology. Import T([G]_P)=⋃_N T_{n_P^N} from AF.0/uniform-moderate-growth-space: a single exponent N controls all derivatives, with constants depending on X. Give the comparison T=⋃_N(L²_{n_P^{-N}})^∞=⋃_N(T₀,n_P^N)^∞ with its specified nonstrict union topology. These unions do not assert equality at the same N in every comparison.; Schwartz decay relative to a weight: For a weight w and N≥0 let S_{w,N} be the smooth functions satisfying sup_x n_P(x)^{−N}w(x)^r|R(X)φ(x)|<∞ for every r≥0 and X. Define S_w=⋃_N S_{w,N} with its nonstrict locally convex union topology. The order of quantifiers is ∃N∀r∀X. Equivalently S_w=⋃_N⋂_{r≥0}(L²_{n_P^{-N}w^r})^∞, allowing an adjustment of N between the two descriptions. At each fixed N,J the displayed seminorms give the Fréchet topology.; Nuclearity and product decompositions: For each finite level J the spaces S([G]_P)^J and C([G]_P)^J are nuclear Fréchet. For two quotient data and product finite level J₁×J₂, multiplication of pure tensors induces topological isomorphisms S(X₁)^J₁⊗̂πS(X₂)^J₂≅S(X₁×X₂)^{J₁×J₂}, and the analogous C isomorphism. Use compatible product heights and product quotient-volume functions. Continuous sesquilinear or bilinear forms extend by the corresponding completed projective universal property. Passing to all levels must be checked through the strict stage system.; Constant terms and pseudo-Eisenstein extensions: For P⊂Q extend the existing AF.3 constant term CT_P^Q and AS.1 pseudo-Eisenstein EP_P^Q to the following spaces, with their established normalized measures: EP:S₀([G]_P)→S₀([G]_Q), CT:T₀([G]_Q)→T₀([G]_P), EP:S([G]_P)→S([G]_Q), and CT:T_N([G]_Q)→T_N([G]_P). They are adjoint under the integral pairing. There is c>0 such that for every N≥0, φ↦sup_x δ_P^Q(x)^{cN}n_P(x)^N|CT_P^Qφ(x)| is a continuous seminorm on S₀([G]_Q). This weighted estimate does not assert unweighted rapid decay of CTφ along all split-central directions.; Approximation by constant terms: For proper P⊊Q, every N>0,r≥0 and X∈U(g∞), there is a continuous seminorm q on T_N([G]_Q) at each fixed level such that |R(X)(φ−CT_P^Qφ)(x)|≤n_P(x)^N d_P^Q(x)^{−r}q(φ) for all x in the common intermediate quotient. If φ∈L²_w([G]_Q)^∞, there is N>0 such that for every r≥0 the integral over A_Q∞ of |φ(ax)−CT_P^Qφ(ax)|² w(a)δ_Q(a)^{−1}da is ≪_r n_P(x)^N d_P^Q(x)^{−r}. In the integral bound the single N is chosen before all r; the notation w(a) uses the restricted A_Q weight in this assertion.; Weighted constant-term decomposition: For P⊂Q and a weight w on [G]_Q there are weights w_P^−,w_P^+ on [G]_P, comparable with w in the deep P-cusp, for which CT_P^Q:L²_w→L²_{w_P^−} and EP_P^Q:L²_{w_P^+}→L²_w are continuous, including their smooth-vector maps. For weights w,w′ with comparable restrictions w|A_Q∞≍w′|A_Q∞, if w′≪w the map φ↦((CT_P^Qφ)_{P⊊Q},φ) is a closed embedding of smooth L²_w into the product of the proper-parabolic weighted smooth spaces and smooth L²_w′. Under the dual comparison w≪w′, the corresponding sum of EP maps and the identity inclusion is an open surjection onto smooth L²_w. State the choices of weights and comparison constants explicitly at each finite level.

stages.title: Schwartz spectral decompositions and automorphic kernels
stages.description: Extend the existing cuspidal-data decomposition to the weighted function spaces, with exact summability and common-height-loss quantifiers. Prove Schwartz relative-character convergence, Arthur factorization, regular constant-term bounds and the GL_n regular-data Lapid expansion. Extend automorphic kernels and their grouped Eisenstein spectral expansions to Schwartz tests with uniform weight bounds. Targets: Relative characters of Schwartz functions: Let π be a discrete automorphic representation of a Levi, A_{P,π}(G) its smooth induced space, B a continuous sesquilinear form on that space, and Ω a compact subset of a_P^{G,*}. For f∈S(G(𝔸)) and a K-orthonormal basis 𝔅, Σ_{v∈𝔅}I_P(λ,f)v⊗overline(v) converges absolutely in A_{P,π}⊗̂π overline(A_{P,π}), uniformly on Re λ∈Ω. The resulting tensor and J_B(λ,f)=Σ_v B(I_P(λ,f)v,v) are basis independent. For each fixed finite support/level stage there is a continuous seminorm p with |J_B(λ,f)|≤p(f) throughout that strip. The functional also extends to C_c^r at sufficiently large r, with derivative degree bounded by r. The basis is a union of finite-dimensional K-type orthonormal bases.; Arthur’s finite differentiability factorization: Fix a normal compact open K₀⊂K_f and m≥1. There exist Z∈U(g∞), g₁∈C_c∞(G(𝔸)) and g₂∈C_c^m(G(𝔸)), all invariant under K∞-conjugation and g_i bi-K₀-invariant, such that every bi-K₀ Schwartz f satisfies f=f*g₁+(f*Z)*g₂. For m sufficiently large, J_B(λ,f) equals the sum of the two absolutely convergent basis sums B(I_P(λ,f)v,I_P(overline λ,g₁^∨)v) and B(I_P(λ,f*Z)v,I_P(overline λ,g₂^∨)v), where g^∨(x)=overline(g(x^{-1})). The choice of Z,g_i depends on K₀,m and not on f; K∞-invariance of Z does not assert that Z is central in U(g∞).; Cuspidal support in weighted function spaces: Import X(G), the Weyl-associate normalized cuspidal data, from AS.1/cuspidal-datum-space, and its orthogonal decomposition from AS.4. If a weight factors through A_P∞, define L²_{w,X} as the orthogonal sum of the blocks indexed by X⊂X(G); these projections agree for different such weights on intersections. Define S_X=S∩L²_X. For an arbitrary quotient weight and F∈{L²_w,C,T_N,T,S_{w,N},S_w}, define F_X as the annihilator of S_{Xᶜ} under the integral pairing. The notation therefore records cuspidal support, not necessarily Hilbert orthogonality for that weight. CT and EP preserve this support with the finite-to-one map X(M_P)→X(G).; Continuous cuspidal-support projections: For every weight w and support subset X, the projection on S extends continuously to (L²_w)^∞→(L²_{w,X})^∞; the family of singleton components is unconditionally summable to φ in that smooth space. On S the sum is absolutely summable. The maps also extend continuously to C,T,S_w and obey ⟨φ_X,ψ⟩=⟨φ,ψ_X⟩ for T×S. There is a common height loss N₀>0 such that singleton components of φ∈T_w are absolutely summable in T_{w n_P^{N₀}}, and those of φ∈S_{w,N} in S_{w,N+N₀}; on C absolute summability holds in C. S_X is dense in C_X and smooth L²_{−N,X}. Under product quotient tensor identifications the X₁×X₂ projection is the completed tensor product of the two projections, giving S_X and C_X product isomorphisms.; Regular cuspidal data: A normalized cuspidal datum represented by (M_P,π) is regular if its stabilizer in W(P)=Norm_G(M_P)/M_P is trivial: wπ≅π implies w=1. This is independent of the chosen Weyl-associate representative. For GL_n and π=⊠_iπ_i on ∏_iGL_{n_i}, regularity means the factors of the same rank are pairwise nonisomorphic; different ranks cannot be permuted. This is not the distinct-parameter condition on a single infinitesimal character and is different from the GGP-specific starred regularity condition.; Regular-support constant terms and holomorphy: If χ is regular, the constant term extends boundedly from L²_χ([G]) to L²_χ([G]_P), and the adjoint pseudo-Eisenstein map is bounded in the reverse direction. For φ∈S_χ([G]) and Re s>0, the Levi function m↦δ_P(m)^{s−1/2}φ_P(m) belongs to C_{χ_M}([M_P]), where χ_M is the finite inverse image support in X(M_P). The family S_χ→C_{χ_M} is holomorphic in s on Re s>0 in the locally convex sense. At the boundary Re s=0 no such C-valued assertion is made.; Lapid expansion of Harish-Chandra Schwartz functions: Let G be a finite product of Res_{K_i/F}GL_{n_i} and χ a regular datum represented by (M_P,π). Write Π=I_P^Gπ. There is N>0 such that for every φ∈C([G]) and λ∈ia_P*, the series φ_{Πλ}=Σ_{v∈𝔅}⟨φ,E(v,λ)⟩ E(v,λ) is defined, basis independent, and converges absolutely in T_N([G]). The map λ↦φ_{Πλ} is Schwartz with values in T_N, using all parameter derivatives, and if φ∈C_χ then φ=∫_{ia_P*}φ_{Πλ}dλ. The exponent N is uniform in λ and φ. The statement for arbitrary reductive groups requires Lapid’s hereditary property (HP); it is not asserted unconditionally here.; Schwartz convolution kernels and cuspidal parts: For f∈S(G(𝔸)) define K_{f,P}, K_{f,P,χ} as the smooth integral kernels of R_P(f) and its χ support component on the AA quotient L² spaces. Define K⁰ on the A_P∞-quotient using its δ_P^{1/2} normalization. They satisfy K⁰_{f,P,χ}(x,y)=∫_{A_P∞}K_{f,P,χ}(x,ay)δ_P(a)^{−1/2}da. This construction extends the compactly supported kernels of AS.6 and fixes its pairing convention by (R_P(f)φ)(x)=∫K_{f,P}(x,y)φ(y)dy. Smooth representatives are used; kernel columns come from regularizing δ_y with the appropriate adjoint. Derivatives in either variable agree with the corresponding left/right derivatives of f.; Uniform bounds for cuspidal kernel parts: There exists N₀>0 such that for every weight w on [G]_P and continuous seminorm q on T_{w n_P^{N₀}} there is a continuous Schwartz seminorm p satisfying Σ_χq(K_{f,P,χ}(·,y))≤p(f)w(y)^{−1}. In particular Σ_χ|K_{f,P,χ}(x,y)|≤p(f)n_P(x)^{N₀}w(x)/w(y). The same pointwise bound holds for Σ_χ|K⁰_{f,P,χ}(x,y)| when x,y∈[G]_P¹=H_P^{-1}(0). The exponent N₀ is chosen before the weight and seminorm.; Spectral expansion of Schwartz kernels: There exist a continuous seminorm p on S(G(𝔸)) and N≥0 such that for every X,Y∈U(g∞), f∈S and x,y∈G(𝔸)¹, the sum over χ and standard P, with coefficient |𝒫(M_P)|^{−1}, of ∫_{ia_P^{G,*}}Σ_τ |Σ_{v∈𝔅_{P,χ,τ}} R_x(X)E(x,I_P(λ,f)v,λ) overline(R_y(Y)E(y,v,λ))|dλ is at most p(L(X)R(Y)f)n_G(x)^Nn_G(y)^N. Here 𝒫(M_P) is the finite set of parabolics with Levi M_P and 𝔅 is a K-basis in the discrete inducing space with support χ. For arbitrary x,y∈G(𝔸), K⁰_{f,χ}(x,y) is the sum of the same undifferentiated Eisenstein terms with those coefficients and spectral measures. The absolute value is outside the finite sum within each K-type, before summing types and integrating.

stages.title: Typical cuspidal data and finite archimedean selection
stages.description: Define T-characters, CAP characters, T-multipliers and quasi-cuspidality. Use both the compact-central condition and derived Casimir condition for typical data. Obtain finite-rank Casimir values, finite typical data and sharp archimedean annihilators of all but finitely many coarse cuspidal components. Targets: Level and T-characters: Fix a number field F, connected reductive G/F, its maximal F-split central torus Z and unitary automorphic central character ω. Fix a finite set S of finite primes containing all ramified group and level places, K=K_S×∏_{v∉S}K_v, and a set T⊃S that may be infinite. H_G^T is the restricted tensor product of the spherical algebras at v∉T, with unit 1_{K_v} and vol(K_v)=1. A T-character χ is a character of Z(g∞)⊗H_G^T, equivalently an infinitesimal-character W-orbit χ∞ and a family of unramified characters away from T. L²_ω[χ] denotes the closed χ-eigenpart in the fixed-level Hilbert space; its cuspidal subspace is intersected with L²_cusp. The normalizations of Z, A_M∞ and unitary unramified twists are compared with AS.1–AS.4.; CAP characters relative to T: For a fixed inner form G′ of G, a T-character χ is (G′,T)-CAP if there is a proper parabolic P′⊊G′ with Levi M′, and a cuspidal automorphic representation σ of M′(𝔸) such that at almost all v∉T the unramified representation determined by χ_v is a constituent of the normalized induction of σ_v, under the unramified inner-form identification. This is an almost-everywhere finite-place condition, independent of χ∞. Non-CAP is its negation. The inner form is a parameter, not an additional existential quantifier. For the non-CAP isolation theorem specialize G′=G and rule out proper cuspidal data of G itself.; Mixed archimedean and spherical multipliers: A T-multiplier is an element of (M♯θ)^W⊗_ℂH_G^T, acting on fixed-K test functions by the real multiplier in the archimedean factor and spherical convolution in the retained finite factors. Its action is continuous stagewise, remains bi-K-invariant, and obeys R(μ⋆f)=μ(χ)R(f) on an irreducible χ-isotypic representation. Evaluation μ(χ) is well defined on the tensor product. This algebra need not have a unit because the sharp factor may not have one; the Hecke unit alone is not an allowed T-multiplier.; Quasi-cuspidal Schwartz test functions: For the fixed (G,Z,ω,K), a bi-K Schwartz test function f is quasi-cuspidal if R(f) maps the entire Hilbert space L²_ω([G]/K) into its closed cuspidal subspace. This is a property of the integrated operator on that quotient and central character. It does not require every local constant term of f to vanish, nor does it quantify over all central characters.; Typical cuspidal data at an infinitesimal character: For each standard Levi M import the splitting of its Cartan dual into a central quotient c_M*/a_M* and the derived Cartan quotient b_M*. Let γ_M^+,γ_M^− be the corresponding quotient maps, and let λ_M be the derived Casimir polynomial. A normalized cusp representation σ of M is χ∞-typical if γ_M^+(χσ∞) belongs to the finite image γ_M^+(χ∞) and λ_M(γ_M^−(χσ∞)) belongs to the finite set λ_M(γ_M^−(χ∞)). Images of W-orbits are finite sets; choices of representatives do not change membership. Work modulo unitary unramified twists on a_M. Fix a finite set of archimedean K_M-types and a compact open finite level when asserting finiteness.; Finite-rank cuspidal Casimir values: At fixed finite level and a finite set of archimedean K_M-types, the set Λ_M of derived Casimir values of cuspidal representations of M modulo a_M twists is countable and has finite rank as a subset of ℂ. More precisely the needed derived semisimple cuspidal counting function, counted with multiplicity below positive elliptic spectral parameter R, is bounded by C(1+R)^d. To pass from M to M_der, one must use a finite union of conjugate finite levels; the original level intersection alone is not sufficient. Normalize the Casimir sign so that its K-type-adjusted elliptic eigenvalue is nonnegative.; Finiteness of typical cuspidal data: For each Levi M, fixed ω, fixed finite level and finite K_M-type set, only finitely many χ∞-typical cuspidal representations occur modulo the normalized a_M twists. After fixing ω and normalizing the a_M twists, the allowed central differentials lie in a discrete affine lattice coset in the remaining central directions of c_M,ℂ*/a_M,ℂ*, possibly of rank zero; the first typicality condition restricts them to finitely many values; the remaining finite-component central characters are finite at the fixed level. Donnelly’s bound restricts derived parameters, and fixed infinitesimal/central-character admissibility gives the final finite representation set.; Archimedean annihilators of unwanted families: For each standard Levi M there is μ∞^M∈(M♯θ)^W with μ∞^M(χ∞)≠0 that vanishes on every induced character χ^G_{σ_s∞} for every complex s∈a_M,ℂ* whenever σ has the fixed permitted types and level and is not χ∞-typical. Construct it using finite-rank interpolation in the derived Casimir and interpolation on the allowed affine central lattice coset in c_M,ℂ*/a_M,ℂ*. Multiply by a sharp symbol μ∞⁰ nonzero at every target Weyl translate; the additional moderate factors alone need not be sharp.; Finite surviving cuspidal components: For the fixed (G,Z,ω,K,χ∞) there exists μ∞∈(M♯θ)^W with μ∞(χ∞)≠0 such that, for every fixed-K Schwartz f, R(μ∞⋆f) has image in a finite orthogonal sum of AS.1 cuspidal-data components. The list is independent of f. Choose the finite detecting K∞-types supplied by μ∞⁰, propagate them to the finitely many Levi K_M-types and finite levels, retain only typical data, and annihilate all remaining data by the product of μ∞^M.

stages.title: Mixed multipliers and isolation of cuspidal components
stages.description: Define simultaneous occurrence at infinity and every retained finite place. Construct mixed annihilators, normalize at the target character, and isolate occurring components. Deduce non-CAP isolation, isolation within the cuspidal domain, preservation of a non-CAP admissible representation, the single GL_n cuspidal-support component, and the discrete-data refinement subject to its explicit counting contract. Targets: Occurrence in a cuspidal datum: A T-character χ occurs in a normalized cuspidal datum (M,σ) if there is one complex parameter s∈a_M,ℂ* for which the induced infinitesimal character equals χ∞ and, for every finite v outside T, the spherical constituent of the normalized induction I_P^G(σ_s,v) has character χ_v. The same parameter must work at all these places. This property descends to the AS.1 Weyl-and-twist equivalence class. Denote the resulting set by D(G,ω)_χ. Occurrence is stronger than the almost-everywhere finite-place condition in CAP.; Mixed archimedean and Hecke annihilators: If χ does not occur in (M,σ), construct a T-multiplier μ_{M,σ} nonzero at χ whose operator annihilates the whole AS.1 cuspidal component L²_(M,σ). Only finitely many places outside T are used, even if T is infinite. For proper M choose representatives α_σ,α_χ and a splitting ℓ:h*→a_M*. For each w∈W the only candidate parameter compatible with α_σ+s=wα_χ is s_w=ℓ(wα_χ)−ℓ(α_σ). Nonoccurrence supplies an invariant archimedean polynomial or a spherical Hecke element at a retained finite place distinguishing the target from that candidate. Its values along the induced family are exponential polynomials in s. A finite linear combination avoiding the finitely many target-zero hyperplanes, followed by a Weyl product, vanishes on the entire family and is nonzero at χ. Multiply by a moderate damping and a sharp seed to obtain an element of (M♯θ)^W⊗H_G^T.; Isolation of occurring cuspidal components: For every T-character χ and the fixed (G,Z,ω,S,K), there is a T-multiplier μ with μ(χ)=1 such that for every f∈S(G(𝔸))^K the image of R(μ⋆f) on L²(G(F)\G(𝔸)/K,ω) lies in the Hilbert orthogonal sum of the AS.1 cuspidal components indexed by D(G,ω)_χ. The constructed range is already contained in a finite sum of these components. The identity μ(χ)=1 preserves the action of f on any admissible representation with this T-character, including one absent from the automorphic spectrum. This theorem asserts a range constraint and scalar normalization; it does not assert that μ acts as the identity on each entire surviving component.; Isolation of non-CAP cuspidal spectrum: If χ is not (G,T)-CAP, choose the normalized multiplier of global isolation so that for every fixed-K Schwartz f its operator on the entire central-character L² space has image in L²_cusp[χ]. In particular μ⋆f is ω-quasi-cuspidal and μ(χ)=1. Without the non-CAP hypothesis the same normalized multiplier has this range property after restricting its domain to L²_cusp. Here L²_cusp[χ] is the maximal closed cuspidal subspace on whose smooth vectors Z(g)⊗H_G^T acts by χ; neither assertion requires χ to be automorphic.; Preservation of a non-CAP admissible representation: Let π be an irreducible admissible representation of G(𝔸) with unitary automorphic central character. Suppose π is not nearly equivalent to a constituent of induction from any proper cuspidal datum. At a finite level K choose finite S containing every ramified place of G, K and π and take T=S. The normalized isolation multiplier satisfies π(μ⋆f)=π(f) for every fixed-K Schwartz f, and its global L² operator has image in the π-nearly isotypic cuspidal subspace. The sharper χπ^T-eigenspace range may be used as an intermediate inclusion. If the nearly isotypic cuspidal subspace is zero, the global L² action is zero while the action on π is still preserved.; Isolation of one GLₙ cuspidal-support component: For G=Res_{F′/F}GL_n and an irreducible admissible π occurring as a constituent of normalized induction of a cuspidal representation σ of a Levi M, with unitary automorphic central character, there is a normalized multiplier preserving π(f) and mapping the entire central-character L² space into the single AS.1 cuspidal-support component attached to (M,σ), for every fixed-K Schwartz f. The correct uniqueness input is the isobaric strong multiplicity-one theorem: the almost-everywhere unramified characters determine the multiset of cuspidal constituents, with their unramified norm twists. It identifies the cuspidal datum, not every irreducible constituent of its induced representation.; Isolation of refined discrete-data components: Replace AS.1 cuspidal data by AS.4 Langlands data (M,σ) with σ in the discrete automorphic spectrum of M, using its normalized unramified-twist and Weyl equivalence. Assuming the polynomial fixed-level, fixed-K-type discrete-spectrum Casimir counting input R8D, there is a T-multiplier with value 1 at χ whose L² range lies in the sum of the refined Langlands components where χ occurs, defined by the same simultaneous character equations. This can be strictly smaller than the coarse cuspidal-support range. The extra polynomial counting theorem is a required input, not a consequence of mere discreteness or of a general trace-class ideal theorem.
